correctness.rationale: Dihedral averaging preserves the feasible symmetric stochastic matrices and lowers the convex norm, so optimizing the two edge weights suffices for the global value. Each Fourier block is (1-beta)I plus entries -2 alpha d on the rim diagonal and beta off-diagonal. Its larger nonstationary eigenvalue at d=delta strictly decreases with beta for alpha>0, so beta=1-2alpha minimizes this lower bound. On that boundary lambda_+(d) decreases and -lambda_-(d) is bounded by sqrt(beta^2+4 alpha^2)=lambda_+(2); this also bounds |1-2beta| since the squared difference is 4 alpha(1-2alpha). The bound is attained for every boundary pair, including the endpoints. For D=4+delta^2, the scalar norm squared is D(alpha-2/D)^2+delta^2/D. Its second derivative is positive; the derivative of the full objective runs from -delta to 2 at the two endpoints. The proposed alpha solves the unsquared stationary equation with norm sqrt(delta)/2, so both weights and the objective are correct, and only uniqueness within the invariant family is asserted. This check applies to the triangle and both parities (only d<=2 is needed). The m=4 substitution gives (3/10,2/5,4/5); expanding delta=2 sin^2(pi/m) yields the stated asymptotics. The uploaded program and frozen numerical output were read, not executed; the universal certificate is RESULT.md lines 35–107, not the sampled spectral tests.
